threads.body: [General] Keeping only the latest chunk discards response data that appeared earlier. Streaming providers can emit choices/finish reasons and usage metadata on different chunks (including a final usage-only chunk); in that case the final synthesized telemetry has no choices, output events, or finish reasons even though content was buffered. Accumulate the per-choice terminal generations and response metadata across chunks, then end the instrumenter with an aggregated response.

replies.body: Fixed in 38ba67dbfc. Streaming state now accumulates per-choice generations and finish reasons, plus response id/model/usage across chunks. The integration test now ends with a usage-only chunk to verify earlier choices and metadata are preserved.

threads.body: [General] When only experimental span-attribute capture is enabled, this buffer still retains the entire streamed response even though serialization later keeps at most the configured maximum. A long stream can therefore consume unbounded memory and defeats the size limit. Bound each builder to the configured limit (with surrogate-boundary handling) unless full log-event content capture is enabled.

replies.body: Fixed in 38ba67dbfc. Per-choice content buffers are bounded by the configured span-attribute limit when only experimental span attributes are enabled, while full log-event capture remains unbounded. The truncation path handles surrogate boundaries and is covered by a split-surrogate streaming test.

threads.body: [General] On failures (`response == null`) or responses without model metadata, this records the requested model as `gen_ai.response.model`. A requested alias may resolve to another model, and no response model exists on failure, so this produces inaccurate span and metric dimensions. Return a response model only when response metadata supplies one.

replies.body: Fixed in 38ba67dbfc. The response model is now emitted only when non-empty response metadata provides it; it no longer falls back to the request model. Exact error-span assertions verify that no response model is present on failures.

threads.body: [Testing] Use `hasAttributesSatisfyingExactly(...)` here. The non-exact assertion silently accepts unexpected attributes, so this aggregation test would not detect accidental or privacy-sensitive attributes added to the span.

threads.body: `ChatResponseMetadata` defaults `usage` to `new EmptyUsage()`, whose token getters return 0. So when a provider returns metadata without setting usage, `getUsageInputTokens`/`getUsageOutputTokens` return `0L` instead of null and the span records `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens=0` and `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens=0`. `GenAiClientMetrics` only null-checks these attributes, so zero-valued `gen_ai.client.token.usage` points get emitted as well. Suggest normalizing the empty-usage sentinel to null here so both getters are covered.

threads.body: [General] `Flux.defer` reads only the subscription thread-local context in `start()`. Reactor invokes the defer supplier during subscription assembly, before its signal callbacks restore the OpenTelemetry context, so a publisher subscribed with its parent only in Reactor `Context` (as commonly happens in WebFlux after the original scope has closed) creates a root or otherwise mis-parented GenAI span. Read the subscriber context with `deferContextual` and use its stored OpenTelemetry context as the parent.

The module check passes on JDK 21, and the default, experimental, and content-disabled suites pass on a JDK 17 test JVM.

Scoping the marker to the delegate invocation at subscription time would keep `deferredStreamDelegateEndsOneSpan` passing without swallowing legitimate nested calls.

This exception-class fallback is generic GenAI behavior, not Spring AI behavior. The shared HTTP, database, messaging, and RPC extractors each set `error.type` themselves rather than leaving it to every library module.

Setting it in `GenAiAttributesExtractor.onEnd()` would give Spring AI, OpenAI, Bedrock, and future GenAI instrumentations the same behavior, and this class could then go away.

Catching `Throwable` inside the helper hides serialization failures from every caller, including the advice paths that already declare `suppress = Throwable.class`.

Only the Reactor completion path runs outside advice, so the suppression belongs at that boundary in `SpringAiStreamTracing`, where it still has to guarantee that `instrumenter.end()` runs. The comment then becomes unnecessary. (Same pattern in `setOutputMessages` below and in `SpringAiMessageEvents`.)

threads.body: [General] This key is not independently sufficient to suppress nested GenAI spans. The AWS Bedrock instrumenter also has `RPC_CLIENT` via `RpcClientAttributesExtractor` (`AwsSdkInstrumenterFactory.java:81-82,411-420`), while `SpanSuppressors.BySpanKey` suppresses only when every key on the inner instrumenter is present. A Spring AI parent stores `GEN_AI_CLIENT` but not `RPC_CLIENT`, so Spring AI calls backed by Bedrock still produce duplicate GenAI client spans. Make an existing `GEN_AI_CLIENT` key sufficient to suppress a mixed-key GenAI instrumenter and add that mixed-key case to the suppression test.

replies.body: Addressed in ffc4eb92cd. For instrumenters that include GEN_AI_CLIENT, an existing GEN_AI_CLIENT key is now independently sufficient for suppression, including the Bedrock-style GEN_AI_CLIENT + RPC_CLIENT combination. Non-GenAI instrumenters retain the existing all-key behavior. Regression coverage includes the real RPC attributes extractor and verifies that RPC-only parents and ordinary RPC instrumenters are not incorrectly suppressed.

threads.body: [General] Preserve the original publisher when request setup fails. `SpringAiRequest.create()` calls the application-provided `getDefaultOptions()`, which can throw (the test fixture already models this). Because this exit advice assigns its return value back to the instrumented method, relying on advice suppression can replace a valid `Flux` with the advice method's default `null` value instead of leaving application behavior unchanged.

replies.body: Addressed in ffc4eb92cd. Request setup and publisher wrapping now run in a helper that explicitly catches and logs instrumentation failures and returns the original publisher. The regression test makes getDefaultOptions() throw, verifies the application response is still delivered, and confirms subsequent stream instrumentation works without advice failures. Base-dependency tests and all latest-dependency variants (Spring AI 1.1.3) pass.

threads.body: Will anything fail when this is removed or are you trying to future proof this?

replies.body: This is an existing failure mode, not just future-proofing. Removing this special case makes `GenAiAttributesExtractorTest.suppressesNestedGenAiInstrumenters(true)` fail: the Bedrock instrumenter uses both `GEN_AI_CLIENT` and `RPC_CLIENT`, while an outer Spring AI instrumenter stores only `GEN_AI_CLIENT`. The regular all-keys rule would therefore start a duplicate nested Bedrock GenAI span. I re-ran that mixed-key regression test after merging the latest `main`, and it passes with this check in place.
